I.    Introduction and Summary
       4K Land and Cattle Company (“4K Land”) respectfully submits this Reply Brief to respond
to the Initial Briefs filed by the Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission
Services Corporation (collectively, “Applicants”), Public Utility Commission of Texas (“PUC” or
“Commission”) Commission Staff (“Staff”), and intervenors supporting Route 894, Route 487, or
other routes that use Links M12, M11, K52, or K51. The initial briefs filed by these parties confirm
the central point made in 4K Land’s Initial Brief: the Applicants have asked the Administrative
Law Judges (“ALJs”) and the Commission to endorse Route 894 without the transparent,
reproducible, and complete analysis necessary to support a best-meets finding for a first-of-its-
kind 765-kV transmission project crossing more than 200 miles of Texas Hill Country and
ranchland.
       The Applicants and Route 894 supporters repeatedly argue that Route 894 performs well
on selective Environmental Assessment table metrics, principally cost, habitable structures, and
the Environmental Assessment’s half-mile foreground-zone metric for parks and recreational

 areas. 1 Those arguments do not answer 4K Land’s overarching application challenge because they
do not supply a disclosed weighting framework, sensitivity testing, a visual-resource or viewshed
analysis, a quantitative terrain analysis, or the missing field-level comparison of the Northern
Corridor and Route 894 corridor in McCulloch County. The Applicants and Route 894 supporters
miss the critical issue 4K Land has raised—the record does not answer the question it was built to
answer.

894 corridor before the Application was filed. 5 And the Environmental Assessment and Routing

894, and the ALJs should evaluate the entire record, including the verifiable field-level and expert

uniquely balanced basis to compare both corridors based on firsthand ownership and management

            For the reasons discussed herein and in its Initial Brief, 4K Land respectfully requests that
the ALJs recommend that the Commission reject Route 894, reject Staff’s Route 487, reject any

that the Application does not support a defensible route-selection decision for a project of this
scale without a more complete, route-wide, standards-based analysis.


II.        Route 894’s “Best-Meets” Label Has No Special Weight and Cannot Substitute for

route that best meets the applicable routing factors, but it also acknowledges that the Commission,
not the Applicants, has the prerogative to select a route for construction. 12 That acknowledgement
is important because the preferred-route label is not evidence and does not carry special weight
under SOAH Order No. 1. 13 The Applicants’ own discovery response confirms that all 122 filed
routes are acceptable to the Applicants and that the Applicants do not oppose selection of any filed

            The Applicants contend that 4K Land’s request for a reproducible methodology is
inconsistent with the Commission’s historic practice because route selection is not a mathematical
exercise. 15 That argument mischaracterizes 4K Land’s position. 4K Land does not ask the
Commission to replace judgment with arithmetic; it asks the Commission to require a record that
allows judgment to be exercised on a disclosed, auditable, and route-wide basis. 16 A process can
preserve Commission discretion while still documenting what criteria were considered, how
competing criteria were balanced, and whether a preferred outcome remains stable under
reasonable alternative assumptions.
            4K Land performed exactly that work, to a nationally recognized, proven standard, and
weighed the routing factors against one another, as the environmental-planning discipline requires
and as the statute’s interdependent factors demand. Mr. Scott applied an EPRI-GTC-based multi-
criteria suitability methodology adapted to the Texas statutory criteria—the very analyses the
Applicants admitted they did not perform—and produced a disclosed, route-wide ranking that the
Commission can audit. The Applicants’ quarrel, then, is not with weighing. It is with a weighing
the Commission can check—and on this record, only 4K Land’s can be.
            The problem here is not that Applicants declined to use a rigid formula. The problem is
that the Applicants did not document any disciplined basis by which Route 894 emerged as
superior to the other 121 acceptable routes. The Applicant produced 122 routes and called them
all adequate. But if every route is adequate, adequacy has chosen nothing. A screen that passes
every candidate has not selected among them—it has only confirmed that each could be built. The
statute does not singularly ask whether a line can be built. It directs the Commission to consider
certain factors and to identify the route that best meets them. 4K Land expert witness Mr. James
E. Scott explained the consequence of unfettered “discretion” as the Applicants would have it: a
routing analysis whose weights are unconstrained cannot demonstrate that the resulting route best
meets the criteria, because the criteria are operationalized in the decisions the Applicants chose

 parochial while relying on their own link-specific exclusions. For example, CE Stephens asks the
 Commission to reject routes using Link N4; Hodge-Schwertner argues that Links E6 and E12 are
 habitable-structure outliers that should disfavor routes using them; and U3 Landowners ask the
 Commission to reject every route using Link U3.22 These arguments confirm that link-level harms
 should be considered when they bear on route-wide statutory and regulatory criteria. 4K Land’s

IV.        Route 894’s Narrow Desktop Advantages Do Not Overcome the Mandatory
           Qualitative Factors
            Route 894’s supporters repeatedly state that Route 894 has favorable cost and habitable-
structure metrics. 4K Land does not dispute that cost and habitable structures are relevant
considerations. 31 But the statute and Commission’s rules also require consideration of community
values, recreational and park areas, historical and aesthetic values, environmental integrity, cost,
engineering constraints, impact moderation, paralleling, use of natural or cultural features, and
prudent avoidance. 32 No one factor controls, and the Applicants’ own “best-meets” label cannot
elevate cost and habitable structures above the factors the Legislature and Commission made
mandatory. 33
            Even on the Applicants’ own metrics, Route 894’s advantages are narrow. Route 894’s
estimated transmission line cost of $1,680,919,000 is 2.7% above the least expensive filed route,
and its 85 habitable structures are only five more than the minimum count of 80 for filed Routes
430 and 442. 34 The narrow cost range and Route 894’s position only 2.7% above the floor show
the thinness of the quantitative basis for declaring a single route “best.” 35 Mr. Scott also testified
that Route 894 ranks 83rd under his comprehensive statutory framework, while Routes 410 and
416 tie for first and Route 392 ranks third. 36
            The evidence demonstrates why the ALJs should not let small tabular differences control
the route decision. A route that appears favorable on cost and habitable structures may still fail to
moderate landowner and community impacts, may still impose severe visual impacts, may still
fragment contiguous ranch operations, may still disregard state-park and scenic-resource concerns,

VII.         Mr. King’s Firsthand Testimony Supplies the Field-Level Comparison the Applicants
             and Route 894 Supporters Lack
             Mr. King’s testimony is uniquely probative because he owns and manages land along
  multiple corridors in McCulloch County. 65 He does not advocate for a route that affects only
  someone else’s land while sparing his own; he compares two corridors that both materially affect
  4K Ranch. 66
             Mr. King testified that the Northern Corridor routes, including Routes 416, 410, 392, 402,
  391, 589, 592, 74, 93, and 100, generally run close to large highways, including U.S. Highway
  190, and appear superior based on Mr. Scott’s analysis. 67 Mr. King then provided the ground-truth
  comparison missing from the Applicants’ analysis. He testified that the Northern Corridor along
  the 4K Ranch contains gently rolling rangeland, accessible terrain, minimal steep grades,
  established ranch roads, less erosion-prone soils, and fewer sensitive riparian crossings. 68 He
  testified that the Route 894 corridor across the 4K Ranch is rougher, more eroded, and contains
